message.content:
The physical answer is: 'It is a "yes," provided the inverse law is not enforced at x=0.'

Assume a laminar Boussinesq natural-convection boundary layer on a vertical surface, with \(x\) measured downstream from the leading edge, \(y\) normal into the fluid, constant fluid properties, and

\[
T_w(x)-T_\infty=\frac{A}{x}.
\]

Then the local temperature excess is

\[
\Delta T_w(x)\sim x^{-1}.
\]

The corresponding local Grashof number is

\[
Gr_x=\frac{g\beta (T_w-T_\infty)x^3}{\nu^2}
      =\frac{g\beta A x^2}{\nu^2},
\]

so \(Gr_x\propto x^2\). For a laminar natural-convection boundary layer,

\[
\frac{\delta}{x}\sim (Pr\,Gr_x)^{-1/4}.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{\delta(x)\propto x^{1/2}}.
\]

The maximum streamwise velocity follows from the usual scaling, e.g.

\[
u_{\max}\sim \frac{\alpha x}{\delta^2}
\]

or equivalently from buoyancy–viscous balance. With \(\delta^2\propto x\),

\[
\boxed{u_{\max}\propto x^0}
\]

so the maximum velocity is essentially independent of \(x\) in the outer similarity region.

The normal velocity at the edge of the boundary layer is set by continuity/displacement of the growing layer:

\[
v(\infty)\sim \frac{u_{\max}\delta}{x}.
\]

Thus

\[
\boxed{v(\infty)\propto x^{-1/2}}.
\]

The local wall heat flux is

\[
q''=-k\left.\frac{\partial T}{\partial y}\right|_{y=0}
    \sim k\frac{T_w-T_\infty}{\delta}
    \sim k\frac{A/x}{x^{1/2}},
\]

so

\[
\boxed{q''\propto x^{-3/2}}.
\]

For a total heat rate per unit width \(Q\) associated with the boundary layer up to a station \(x\), one obtains the same outer scaling as the enthalpy flux in the layer,

\[
Q\sim \rho c_p u_{\max}(T_w-T_\infty)\delta
   \propto x^{-1/2}.
\]

More carefully, if the inverse law is regularized by a finite inner station \(x_0>0\),

\[
Q(x)\sim C\left(x_0^{-1/2}-x^{-1/2}\right),
\]

so the varying part of the outer solution scales as

\[
\boxed{Q\propto x^{-1/2}}.
\]

Summary of the \(x\)-dependences:

| Quantity | Scaling with \(x\) |
|---|---:|
| \(T_w-T_\infty\) | \(x^{-1}\) |
| \(\delta\) | \(x^{1/2}\) |
| \(u_{\max}\) | \(x^0\) |
| \(v(\infty)\) | \(x^{-1/2}\) |
| \(q''\) | \(x^{-3/2}\) |
| \(Q\) | \(x^{-1/2}\), up to an inner-region constant |

This situation is physically obtainable only if the \(1/x\) law is not required to hold all the way to a singular leading edge at \(x=0\). It arises as an outer similarity flow for a vertical surface whose heating is concentrated near the leading edge—for example, a finite line-source or small heated region at the leading edge of a vertical plate, or an externally controlled wall temperature distribution following \(1/x\) for \(x>x_0\). Under those conditions, the far-field natural-convection boundary layer has the scalings above.
